title: Quickstart UI asset pipeline: internationalization-safe crops, brand token overlays, and privacy-blur orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our quickstart and product screenshots are created ad-hoc by multiple teams which produces inconsistent crops, occasional exposure of user-identifying text (emails/IDs), and layout breakage for non-US locales. This increases engineering churn for docs, adds friction to translations, and risks leaking customer data in public-facing assets.

Goal: Define and ship a lightweight image processing pipeline (design + infra + automation) that ingests raw UI captures and outputs brand-consistent assets across locales and aspect ratios. Pipeline must: 1) automatically detect and obfuscate sensitive strings while preserving contextual readability for illustrative screenshots; 2) perform focal-crop and device-framing rules so primary UI elements remain visible across common aspect ratios; 3) apply brand token overlays (corners, badges, color palette) consistently; 4) produce localized variants with language-safe padding and typographic fallbacks; 5) integrate with CMS/docs upload and flag images for manual QA when automated confidence is low.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline spec doc reviewed and approved by Design + Security (link in attachments)
Figma plugin prototype can export raw capture -> processed PNG with branding layer and privacy blur in the expected folder structure
Automated tests for 6 representative locales (en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ko-KR, pt-BR) produce visually valid crops with primary CTA visible
Confidence threshold defined: images with OCR confidence < 90% are flagged and routed to manual QA
Home page quickstart and SDK docs updated with new assets and release notes (release: docs-2026.04)
Observability: SLI for asset processing success rate > 98% and mean processing time < 2s for small images
comments: 2026-03-11 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agreed to prioritize privacy-first handling (blur > redact) for screenshots that may contain emails/IDs. Action: Rafael to build Figma export prototype by 2026-03-18.

2026-03-12 Rafael Ortiz: Initial Figma plugin PoC can mark safe zones and export JSON metadata describing focal regions. Using Tesseract OCR for detection as a stopgap; plan to swap to ENG OCR service (ENG-2987) once available.

2026-03-12 Priya Raman (Security): Reviewed threat model. Recommended: default blur for anything matching email/phone patterns, pseudonymization for names, and K-anonymity fallback for screenshots containing >3 identifiers. Security requested a short doc for audit logs.

2026-03-13 Maya Chen: Design critique session — UI team requested a softened blur to preserve legibility in examples where partial visibility is needed. We decided on two privacy modes: strict (full blur) and illustrative (masked with hashed token overlay). Rafael to implement both and expose toggle in plugin.

2026-03-13 Ethan Park (Docs): Noted downstream requirement: generated assets must include a small metadata JSON with locale, source commit, mask-mode, and processing checksum so the docs pipeline can invalidate caches when images change.
notes: Implementation approach: lightweight node service with imagemagick + cv2 for crop heuristics, OCR for mask detection, and a small rules engine for brand overlay placement. Deliver Figma plugin + CLI to run batch jobs. Plan staged rollout: internal docs -> marketing pages -> public SDK guides. Add visual regression checks using snapshot tooling (Percy/Playwright).
next_steps: Rafael: finalize Figma plugin and share demo during 2026-03-18 design sync
Engineering: schedule OCR service integration with ENG-2987; define API contract for confidence scores
Security: produce short audit checklist for processed assets and retention policy
Docs: prepare migration plan for existing quickstart screenshots and update docs pipeline to read image metadata
